title: The 2017 Goldman Sachs Gives Analyst Impact Fund
description: Teams made up of nearly 300 analysts from Goldman Sachs offices around the world competed to win grants from Goldman Sachs Gives to support innovative non-profit organizations of their choice. The Goldman Sachs Gives Analyst Impact Fund is sponsored by the Partnership Committee, whose mission is to steward the firm’s culture and cultivate our current and future leaders. The initiative provides analysts with the opportunity to collaborate with peers across the firm to make an impact in the communities where we live and work. Learn more: http://link.gs.com/nzc7

The partnership committee started this initiative to more broadly engage our junior professionals who are so important to our businesses and to the long-term success of the firm and to a couple of recurring themes. Strong analytics. Inspired creativity. A deep sense of camaraderie with their teammates. India has the highest number of out-of-school girls and child brides anywhere on the planet. We believe Educate Girls offers the best in-class solutions by mobilising entire communities who were once part of the problem but are now key stakeholders in the solution. Over 40,000 people have been killed by landmines in Cambodia in the past 20 years, of which approximately 1 3rd have been children. Apobo believes and has proven that rats are currently the fastest, cheapest and most efficient alternative for landmine detection. These are giant African pouch rats with a keen sense of smell that are able to detect the explosive TNT in land mines. Pretty impressive, right? There are over 225 million individuals in rural Africa that rely primarily on livestock for their livelihood. These pasteuralists are adversely affected by herd mortality. We propose using the $150,000 grant to launch a mobile application called AfroScout, which would benefit pastoralists by leveraging satellite-generated maps to optimize herd-migration decisions. This program will directly impact 250 people and their dependents. And once proven successful, Somersaults and the IRC are committed to replicating this project in other refugee communities. This has the potential to provide thousands of permanent jobs for displaced people all throughout the world. Every single day, 450,000 people are held in jail without a conviction. When just a single day in jail can cause someone to lose their job or their housing, even custody of their children? That's why we're here. We're here seeking $150,000 investment in the Bronx Freedom Fund, which provides bails of $2000 or less to poor New Yorkers accused of low-level, non-violent offenses. In third place is... The Bronx Freedom Fund, from New York. in second place is... Educate Girls, from Bengaluru and London.
